record.what_it_does: Cloud platform for deploying and hosting web apps, with domains, functions and storage.
record.auth_notes: There are three ways to authenticate. (1) Access tokens: users create personal tokens (prefix vcp_) on the Account Tokens page, or through POST /v3/user/tokens. A token is scoped to the full account, one team or one project, has an expiration, and is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. A full-account token needs `?teamId=` to reach team resources. (2) Integrations (connectable accounts): an OAuth-style install redirect returns a `code`, which is exchanged at POST https://api.vercel.com/v2/oauth/access_token using client_id, client_secret and redirect_uri. Long-lived tokens are deprecated. New integrations should turn on "Issue Only Short-Lived Access Tokens" and get 1-hour tokens through the client_credentials grant for each installation. Integration scopes cover deployment, project, env vars, domain, drains, edge-config, team, user and billing (billing is Pro/Enterprise only). (3) Sign in with Vercel: an OAuth 2.0 + OIDC IdP with PKCE. It authorizes at vercel.com/oauth/authorize and exchanges tokens at api.vercel.com/login/oauth/token. Access tokens last 1 hour; refresh tokens last 30 days and rotate. However, the permissions that let these tokens call the REST API or team resources are "currently in private beta". For now, a multi-user toolkit should therefore use an Integration install or tokens that users paste in.
record.access_notes: The Hobby plan is free ($0/mo). The access-token docs list no plan restriction; the only prerequisite is a Vercel account, though a team may require 2FA or SAML. Integrations are created by filling in the Create Integration form in the Integrations Console. Once submitted, a connectable-account integration gets a "Community" badge and external users can install it from your site or a deploy button. A listing on the public Integrations page needs 500+ active installs and a review. Native (Marketplace) integrations need Vercel's involvement through a shared Slack channel or program sign-up. Sign in with Vercel's REST API permissions are in private beta. Some features are plan-gated: Account Webhooks and the billing scope need Pro or Enterprise.
record.api_breadth_notes: The REST reference index lists about 475 endpoint rows. It covers access groups, AI Gateway, artifacts, billing, bulk redirects, checks, Connect, deployments, DNS, the domains registrar, domains, drains, edge/global config, env vars, feature flags, integrations, the marketplace, auth tokens, KMS, logs, microfrontends, observability, projects, rolling releases, sandboxes, security/firewall, storage, teams, Vercel CI, web analytics, webhooks, aliases and certs. A machine-readable OpenAPI spec is linked at https://vercel.com/openapi.json.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.vercel.com is Vercel's official remote MCP server, using OAuth and Streamable HTTP. It is available on all plans. Clients must use a Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) or be reviewed and approved by Vercel. The docs have moved to https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp.
record.blocker_notes: The REST API is broad and has an OpenAPI spec. Credentials are self-serve: free Hobby accounts can create personal tokens, and Integrations can be self-created and installed by external users with a Community badge. Caveats: long-lived integration tokens are deprecated, so a toolkit should use short-lived client_credentials tokens per installation. Sign in with Vercel's API permissions are in private beta. Account webhooks and the billing scope need Pro or Enterprise. A public marketplace listing needs 500 installs and a review. There is no separate test mode, but a free Hobby account works for testing.
